players.product: Wholesale hyperscale IDC in China (Greater Beijing / Ulanqab campuses) leased to cloud and internet companies, plus retail IDC; 1,007 MW wholesale capacity in service as of June 30, 2026

quarterly_data.signal: 20-F customer and supplier concentration: two entity customers each generated more than 10% but less than 20% of total net revenues in 2025 (one in 2024 and one in 2023); VNET had over 7,000 enterprise customers as of December 31, 2025, over 1,500 of them using managed hosting services, and relies on internet-industry customers for a significant portion of revenues. The five largest suppliers accounted for 46% of total bandwidth and cabinet resources in 2025 (45% in 2024, 42% in 2023); VNET depends on China Telecom, China Unicom and China Mobile for telecommunication resources while competing with them, and buys routers, switches and other equipment from a limited number of suppliers with no guaranteed supply arrangements.
quarterly_data.figure: two customers each more than 10% but less than 20% of 2025 net revenues; five largest suppliers 46% of bandwidth and cabinet resources

quarterly_data.signal: 20-F operating base: total net revenues were RMB9,949.3 million in 2025 (RMB8,259.1 million in 2024, RMB7,412.9 million in 2023; a 15.9% CAGR). Wholesale IDC as of December 31, 2025: 889 MW in service (Greater Beijing Area 578 MW, 65.0%; Yangtze River Delta 311 MW, 35.0%), 848 MW committed (95.3%), 623 MW utilized (70.1%), and 452 MW under construction with 156 MW pre-committed (34.5%). Retail IDC had 49,863 cabinets in service, and average monthly recurring revenue per retail cabinet was RMB9,045 in 2025 (RMB8,769 in 2024).
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 net revenues RMB9,949.3 million; 889 MW wholesale in service (95.3% committed, 70.1% utilized); 452 MW under construction (34.5% pre-committed)

quarterly_data.signal: 20-F capex and commitments: capital expenditures were RMB8,240.0 million in 2025 (RMB4,982.1 million in 2024, RMB3,578 million in 2023); as of December 31, 2025 purchase commitments for machinery, equipment, construction in progress, bandwidth and cabinet capacity of RMB4,000.3 million were due within twelve months.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 capex RMB8,240.0 million (2024 RMB4,982.1 million); RMB4,000.3 million purchase commitments due within twelve months

quarterly_data.signal: 20-F Microsoft partnership: VNET is Microsoft's local partner operating Microsoft Azure, Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365 and Power Platform in the Chinese mainland (public cloud since 2013, hybrid cloud since 2014). VNET signs the service agreements with end customers; billing is divided between Microsoft and VNET under agreed metrics through a jointly administered escrow account settled monthly, VNET earns incentive payments from Microsoft on certain sales or service conditions, and the agreement renews automatically year by year. The filing states that failure to maintain the partnership could materially affect its cloud service business.
